label: thm:B
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:B}
If $p$ does not divide the order of $\mathcal{O}_F^\times/E(\mathfrak{N})$, 
then for an integer $j>0$, 
a Hecke eigensystem occurs in $H^j(Y(\mathfrak{N}),\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p)$ 
if and only if it occurs in $H^0(Y(\mathfrak{N}),\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p)$.
head: environment

label: thm:C
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:C}
If $p$ does not divide the order of $\mathcal{O}_F^\times/E(\mathfrak{N})$, then $H^\bullet(Y(\mathfrak{N}),\mathbb{F}_p)$ is a free graded $\mathbb{T}^\bullet$-module of rank one, generated in degree zero.
head: environment

label: property:torus
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By the proof of \cite[Proposition 2.1 (3)]{KimKwon2024}, the regulator map identifies
the space $E(\mathfrak{N})\backslash F_{\mathbb{R},+}^\times/U$ 
with the product of $\mathbb R$ and an $r$-torus whose first homotopy group is isomorphic to $E(\mathfrak N)$. 
Therefore $E(\mathfrak{N})\backslash F_{\mathbb{R},+}^\times/U$ is a $K(E(\mathfrak{N}),1)$.
As $E(\mathfrak{N})$ is discrete, this proves the assertion.
head: environment

label: torus:copy
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{torus:copy}
The arithmetic torus $Y(\mathfrak{N})$ is homeomorphic to the $\mathrm{Cl}_F^+(\mathfrak{N})$-disjoint union of 
$E(\mathfrak{N})\backslash F^\times_{\mathbb{R},+}/U$ 
under the map $\bigsqcup_{[a]\in\mathrm{Cl}_F^+(\mathfrak{N})}\iota_a$.

label: definition:derived:hecke:algebra
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{definition:derived:hecke:algebra}
Let us denote by $\mathbb{T}_R^\bullet$ the graded $R$-subalgebra of $\mathrm{End}_{R}H^\bullet(Y(\mathfrak{N}),R)$
generated by $\mathbb{T}_{v,R}^\bullet$ for all $v\in T_0$
and $\mathbb T_{v,R}^0$ for all primes $v$ of $F$ coprime to $\mathfrak N$.
We call $\mathbb{T}_R^\bullet$ {\it the derived Hecke algebra} of $Y(\mathfrak{N})$ with coefficients in $R$.
head: environment
name: Derived Hecke algebra, {Venkatesh

title: Remark
body_md:
In the torus case, adding classical Hecke operators at primes dividing $\mathfrak N$
does not enlarge $\mathbb T_R^0$.
Indeed, translation by an idele induces an action on cohomology depending only on
its narrow ray class, and every narrow ray class is represented by a prime coprime to
$\mathfrak N$ by the Chebotarev density theorem.
head: environment

label: Hecke:module:structure
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{Hecke:module:structure}
The following are true:
\begin{itemize}
\item[(1)] $H^0(Y(\mathfrak N),R)=\mathbb T_R^01_1$.
\item[(2)] $\mathbb{T}^0_R=\sum_{z\in \mathbb A_F^\times/\widehat{\mathcal O}_F^\times}Rh_{z,1}$.
\item[(3)] 
$
\mathbb{T}_R^\bullet
=\sum_{m\geq 0}\sum_{\underline{\alpha}}
\mathbb{T}_R^0 h_{1,\underline{\alpha}},
$
where $\underline{\alpha}$ runs over the $m$-copy of
\[
\bigsqcup_{v\in T_0}H^\bullet(O_v^\times,R).
\]
\end{itemize}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The claim (1) follows from equation~\eqref{hecke:action:representation} for $a=1$
and the fact that $H^0(Y(\mathfrak N),R)$ is generated by $1_a$'s.
(2) follows from Lemma~\ref{representative:choice} and equation~\eqref{eq:hecke}.
For (3), $\mathbb{T}_R^\bullet$ is spanned over $R$ by finite products of operators $h_{1,\alpha}h_{z,1}$. 
Then equation~\eqref{eq:comm} allows us to move all degree-zero operators to the left. 
Their product belongs to $\mathbb{T}_R^0$, which proves (3).
head: environment

label: hecke:action:faithful
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{hecke:action:faithful}
The following map is injective:
\[
\mathbb T^\bullet_R\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_R\left(H^0(Y(\mathfrak N),R),H^\bullet(Y(\mathfrak N),R)\right),
\quad
h\longmapsto h\vert_{H^0(Y(\mathfrak N),R)}.
\]
head: environment

label: component:formula
title: Proof
body_md:
Suppose that the restiction of $h\in\mathbb T_R^\bullet$ is zero.
Choose $a\in C(\mathfrak N)$ and $c\in H^\bullet(Y(\mathfrak N),R)$.
For $h=h_{z,1}h_{1,\underline\alpha}$, 
Proposition~\ref{computation:hecke:operator:product}
and equations~\eqref{eq:hecke},~\eqref{eq:comm},~\eqref{hecke:action:representation} give the equations
\[
\iota_a^*(hc)=I_{\mathfrak N}(\underline\alpha)\cup\iota_{z(a)}^*(c),
\quad
\iota_a^*(h1_b)=\delta_{z(a),b}I_{\mathfrak N}(\underline\alpha).
\]
From this, we obtain
\begin{equation}\label{component:formula}
\iota_a^*(hc)
=\sum_{b\in C(\mathfrak N)}\iota_a^*(h1_b)\cup\iota_b^*(c).
\end{equation}
By Proposition~\ref{Hecke:module:structure},
every $h\in\mathbb T_R^\bullet$ is an $R$-linear combination of $h_{z,1}h_{1,\underline\alpha}$.
Therefore, the formula~\eqref{component:formula} extends linearly to every $h\in\mathbb T_R^\bullet$.
From our assumption and Proposition~\ref{torus:copy}, we deduce that $hc=0$. 
As $h\in\mathbb T_R^\bullet$, we obtain that $h=0$.
head: environment

label: hecke:zero:free
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{hecke:zero:free}
                                                                                                          
The map
\[
\mathbb T_R^0\to H^0(Y(\mathfrak N),R),\quad h\mapsto h1_1
\] 
is an isomorphism of $\mathbb T_R^0$-modules.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The map of the statement is surjective 
by Proposition~\ref{Hecke:module:structure} (1). Choose $h\in\mathbb T_R^0$ and assume that $h1_1=0$.
By Proposition~\ref{Hecke:module:structure} and the commutativity of $\mathbb T^0_R$, 
we have $hc=0$ for any $c\in H^0(Y(\mathfrak N),R)$.
By Proposition~\ref{hecke:action:faithful}, we get $h=0$. 
Hence the map $h\mapsto h1_1$ is injective. So we are done.
head: environment

label: injectivity:psi
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{injectivity:psi}
The map $\Psi_R^\bullet$ defined in \eqref{eq:psi} is injective.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Proposition~\ref{hecke:zero:free}, the domain of $\Psi_R^\bullet$ can be identified with $\mathbb T_R^\bullet$.
Under this identification, the map $\Psi_R^\bullet$ can be identified with the map $h\mapsto h1_1$.
Suppose that $h1_1=0$. By using Proposition~\ref{Hecke:module:structure} and~\eqref{eq:comm}, 
we obtain that $hc=0$ for each $c\in H^0(Y(\mathfrak N),R)$. 
By Proposition~\ref{hecke:action:faithful}, we are done.
head: environment

label: dimension:prop
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{dimension:prop}
The image of $\Psi^\bullet$ has $\mathbb{F}_p$-dimension $h_F^+(\mathfrak{N})\cdot d_p$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Proposition~\ref{Hecke:module:structure} (1), 
the image $\operatorname{Im}(\Psi^\bullet)$ coincides with $\mathbb{T}^\bullet 1_1$.
By Proposition \ref{Hecke:module:structure} and equation~\eqref{eq:comm},
\[
\mathbb{T}^\bullet 1_1
=\sum_{m\geq 0}\sum_{\underline\alpha}\mathbb{T}^0 h_{1,\underline\alpha}1_1
=\sum_{a\in C(\mathfrak{N})}\sum_{m}\sum_{\underline\alpha}\mathbb{F}_p h_{1,\underline\alpha}1_a,
\]
where $\underline\alpha$ runs over the $m$-copy of
$\bigsqcup_{v\in T_1}H^\bullet(\kappa_v^\times,\mathbb{F}_p)$.
The summands are linearly disjoint for $a\in C(\mathfrak N)$,
as $h_{1,\underline\alpha}1_a$'s are cohomology classes supported on the distinct connected components.
Therefore, we obtain from the above equation that
\begin{equation*}
\dim_{\mathbb{F}_p}\operatorname{Im}(\Psi^\bullet)
=h_F^+(\mathfrak{N})\cdot\dim_{\mathbb{F}_p}\sum_{m\geq 0}
\sum_{\underline\alpha}\mathbb{F}_p h_{1,\underline\alpha}1_1.
\end{equation*}
By Proposition~\ref{computation:hecke:operator:product}, we have
\begin{equation*}
\iota_b^*(h_{1,\underline{\alpha}}1_a)=\delta_{a,b}I_{\mathfrak{N}}(\underline{\alpha}).
\end{equation*}
Thus under the injection $\iota_1^*$ (Proposition~\ref{torus:copy}), the space on the right maps to
\begin{equation*}
\sum_{m\geq0}\sum_{\underline{\alpha}}\mathbb{F}_p I_{\mathfrak{N}}(\underline{\alpha})
\subset H^\bullet(E(\mathfrak{N}),\mathbb{F}_p)
\end{equation*}
by Proposition~\ref{computation:hecke:operator:product}. Its dimension is $d_p$ by definition. So we are done.
head: environment

label: dimension:tp:dp
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{dimension:tp:dp}
 $2^{t_p}\leq d_p\leq 2^r$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $E(\mathfrak{N})$ is free abelian of rank $r$, 
its cohomology ring is isomorphic to the exterior algebra on $H^1(E(\mathfrak{N}),\mathbb{F}_p)$ 
and has dimension $2^r$.
The subspace defining $t_p$ generates an exterior subalgebra of dimension $2^{t_p}$, 
contained in the graded subalgebra defining $d_p$. So we are done.
head: environment

label: dimension:lemma
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{dimension:lemma}
There is a finite subset $S\subset T_1$ such that the space
\[
\sum_{v\in S}i_{v,\mathfrak N}^*\mathrm{Hom}(\kappa_v^\times,\mathbb{F}_p)
\]
is equal to the space defining $t_p$ and has dimension $r_p-\delta_p$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Denote by $i_v\colon \mathcal{O}_F^\times \to \kappa_v^\times$ the reduction map.
Then $i_{v,\mathfrak N}$ is the restriction of $i_{v}$.
Thus, for a finite subset $T$ of $T_1$, the map
\begin{equation*}
\prod_{v\in T}\mathrm{Hom}(\kappa_v^\times,\mathbb{F}_p)
\longrightarrow\mathrm{Hom}(E(\mathfrak{N}),\mathbb{F}_p),
\quad
(\phi_v)_{v\in T}\longmapsto
\sum_{v\in T}i_{v,\mathfrak N}^*(\phi_v)
\end{equation*}
factors through $\mathrm{Hom}(\mathcal{O}_F^\times,\mathbb{F}_p)$ 
via the map $(\phi_v)_{v\in T}\mapsto\sum_{v\in T}i_v^*(\phi_v)$, 
followed by restriction to $E(\mathfrak N)$.
By \cite[Lemma 4.6]{KimKwon2024}, which is an isomorphism theorem 
induced by Grunwald--Wang theorem, there is a finite subset
$S\subset T_1$ such that the map
$(\phi_v)_{v\in S}\mapsto\sum_{v\in S}i_v^*(\phi_v)$
is an isomorphism onto
$\mathrm{Hom}(\mathcal{O}_F^\times,\mathbb{F}_p)$.
Using the exact sequence
\begin{equation*}
\begin{tikzcd}
0 \arrow{r} & \mathrm{Hom}(\mathcal{O}_F^\times/E(\mathfrak{N}),\mathbb{F}_p) \arrow{r} &  \mathrm{Hom}(\mathcal{O}_F^\times,\mathbb{F}_p) \arrow{r} & \mathrm{Hom}(E(\mathfrak{N}),\mathbb{F}_p),
\end{tikzcd}
\end{equation*}
the assertion of the lemma follows.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: Since $\mathcal{O}_F^\times/E(\mathfrak{N})$ is a finite abelian group, $\delta_p>0$ if and only if $p$ divides $\left |\mathcal{O}_F^\times/E(\mathfrak{N})\right |$. In particular, when $r>0$ and $p$ does not divide $\left | \mathcal{O}_F^\times/E(\mathfrak{N}) \right|$, we have $r_p-\delta_p >0$.
head: environment

label: spectral:degeneracy
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{spectral:degeneracy}
Let $\lambda$ be a Hecke eigensystem on $H^0(Y(\mathfrak{N}),\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p)$.
For every integer $1\leq j\leq r_p-\delta_p$, the restriction 
\[
\mathbb T^j\otimes_{\mathbb T^0} H^0(Y(\mathfrak{N}),\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p)[\lambda]
\longrightarrow
H^j(Y(\mathfrak{N}),\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p)[\lambda],\quad h\otimes c\longmapsto hc
\]
of $\Psi^j$ is well-defined and non-vanishing, where $H^i[\lambda]$'s are the $\lambda$-eigenspaces.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We consider the derived Hecke action with coefficients in $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p$.
The result will be equal to the base change of the derived Hecke action with $\mathbb F_p$-coefficients, as explained in \cite[\textsection 2.12]{venkatesh2016derived}.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                               
Also note that the natural map induces an isomorphism $H^j(Y(\mathfrak{N}),\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p)\simeq H^j(Y(\mathfrak{N}),\mathbb{F}_p)\otimes_{\mathbb{F}_p}\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p$, because $\mathbb F_p \to \overline{\mathbb{F}}_p$ is flat.

Let $\lambda:\mathbb{T}^0\rightarrow\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p$ be a Hecke eigensystem on 
$H^0(Y(\mathfrak{N}),\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p)$ and $c\in H^0(Y(\mathfrak{N}),\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p)$ 
an eigenvector for the given Hecke eigensystem. 
Note that $c$ can be written as a linear combination of $1_a$'s over $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p$. 
Let $1\leq j\leq r_p-\delta_p$.
By Lemma~\ref{dimension:lemma}, we can choose $v_1,\ldots,v_j\in T_1$ and 
$\alpha_i\in H^1(\kappa_{v_i}^\times,\mathbb{F}_p)$ such that
$i_{v_1,\mathfrak{N}}^*(\alpha_1),\ldots,i_{v_j,\mathfrak{N}}^*(\alpha_j)$
are linearly independent in $H^1(E(\mathfrak{N}),\mathbb{F}_p)$.
Since $E(\mathfrak{N})$ is free, its cohomology ring is isomorphic to the exterior algebra on 
$H^1(E(\mathfrak{N}),\mathbb{F}_p)$. Thus, for $\underline{\alpha}=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_j)$,
$I_{\mathfrak{N}}(\underline{\alpha})\neq 0.$
Choose $a\in C(\mathfrak{N})$ with $\iota_a^*(c)\neq 0$.
By Proposition~\ref{computation:hecke:operator:product},
\begin{equation*}
\iota_a^*(h_{1,\underline{\alpha}}c)
=I_{\mathfrak{N}}(\underline{\alpha})\cup\iota_a^*(c)\neq 0.
\end{equation*}
Hence $h_{1,\underline{\alpha}}c$ is a non-zero class in $H^j(Y(\mathfrak{N}),\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p)$.
Then for any $h_0\in\mathbb{T}^0$, Proposition~\ref{Hecke:module:structure} and equation~\eqref{eq:comm} give
$h_0h_{1,\underline{\alpha}}c
=h_{1,\underline{\alpha}}h_0c
=\lambda(h_0)h_{1,\underline{\alpha}}c$.
So we are done.
head: environment

label: modp:nonvanishing
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The first assertion of the theorem follows from Lemma~\ref{dimension:lemma}. 

Suppose first that $\delta_p=r_p-r$. Then $t_p=r$, so Lemma~\ref{dimension:tp:dp} gives $d_p=2^r$.
By Lemma~\ref{dimension:prop}, $\Psi^\bullet$ is surjective, hence an isomorphism by Proposition~\ref{injectivity:psi}.

Conversely, suppose that $\delta_p\neq r_p-r$.
Since $t_p\leq r$, the first assertion implies $t_p<r$.
The dimension formula for $\Psi^1$ was proved in \cite[Lemma 4.3]{KimKwon2024} 
by an argument analogous to the proof of Lemma~\ref{dimension:prop}.
It gives
\begin{equation*}
\dim_{\mathbb{F}_p}\operatorname{Im}(\Psi^1)
=h_F^+(\mathfrak{N})\cdot t_p
<h_F^+(\mathfrak{N})\cdot r
=\dim_{\mathbb{F}_p}H^1(Y(\mathfrak{N}),\mathbb{F}_p).
\end{equation*}
Therefore $\Psi^1$ is not surjective.
Since $\Psi^\bullet$ preserves degrees, it cannot be an isomorphism.
head: environment

label: remark:dimension
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{remark:dimension}
For the condition $\delta_p=r_p-r$ in Theorem\,\ref{modp:nonvanishing} to hold true, 
we have either $\delta_p=r_p-r=1$ or $\delta_p=r_p-r=0$. 
The latter happens exactly when $p$ does not divide $\left|\mathcal{O}_F^\times / E(\mathfrak N)\right|$. 
The former happens exactly when $F$ contains a primitive $p$-th root of unity and $\delta_p=1$.
head: environment

label: cor:4.10
title: Corollary
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Theorem \ref{modp:nonvanishing}, combined with the equation \eqref{dimension:equation:remark}, implies Theorem~\ref{thm:A}.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Recall that we assumed that $F$ is neither $\mathbb Q$ nor an imaginary quadratic field. In particular, $r_p>0$.
Now Theorem~\ref{spectral:degeneracy} and Corollary~\ref{cor:4.10}, combined with the equation \eqref{dimension:equation:remark}, imply Theorem~\ref{thm:B}.
head: environment

body_md: Theorem~\ref{thm:A}, combined with Proposition~\ref{hecke:zero:free}, implies Theorem~\ref{thm:C}.
